title: Learn Together Stop Apart: an Inclusive Approach to Ensemble Pruning

problem.claim: Determining the optimal number of models in an ensemble is a critical problem.

gap.claim: The optimal ensemble size remains underexplored, and universal ensemble-size assumptions may not account for heterogeneous data points.

narrative_sequence.summary: Gradient Boosting builds ensembles, adapts their sizes to particular tasks, and delivers top-tier results across various applications.
Determining the optimal number of ensemble models is critical but underexplored.
Traditional methods assume one ensemble size works for all data points, despite data heterogeneity.

source_observation.claim: A universal ensemble size may not be effective for every data point because data are heterogeneous.

interpretation.claim: Model-complexity choices may need to vary across individual data points rather than being fixed globally.

application.claim: When pruning or sizing ensembles, consider data-dependent ensemble sizes.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not specify when a universal ensemble size is sufficient.

unknowns: The proposed pruning method is not described.
No experimental setup, datasets, metrics, numerical results, or comparisons are supplied.
The abstract units do not state an explicit author-claimed novelty.
